plain_english_policy: This bill expands criminal liability for chemical endangerment to include unborn children (fetuses) at any stage of development. It establishes that if a mother and her newborn baby both test positive for the same un-prescribed drug, there is an automatic legal assumption ('rebuttable presumption') that the fetus was exposed in utero unless proven otherwise.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would criminalize exposing fetuses to controlled substances by establishing them as 'children' under existing chemical endangerment laws. It shifts the burden of proof regarding exposure onto the defendant when a positive drug test is found at birth, and it designates the county where the child is born as the proper location for trial.
sponsorship_supports_position: Representatives McLaughlin and McDaniel advanced this bill to expand criminal protections for unborn children by clarifying legal definitions of 'child' in the context of chemical endangerment.
evidence_quotes: "This bill would clarify the term "child" to include an unborn child in utero at any stage of development regardless of viability."
"A rebuttable presumption of exposure in utero... exists if both the mother and the child test positive for the same controlled substance at the time of birth"
